title: eClerx Services Ltd - 532927 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: eClerx Q4 FY26 operating revenue USD 122M, up 17% YoY but only 0.6% QoQ; FY26 revenue USD 469M, up 17.9%, with FY27 EBITDA guided at 24-28%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue was USD 122 million, up 17% YoY and 0.6% QoQ, with INR revenue of INR 1,135 crores (up 24% YoY). Operating EBITDA was INR 2,841 million at a 25.7% margin, up 2.8% sequentially, and Q4 PAT was INR 1,894 million (16.7% margin). Full-year FY26 operating revenue reached USD 469 million (up 17.9% in USD), with EBITDA up 29% and PAT up 30% to INR 706 crores. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of top-quartile revenue growth and a 24-28% EBITDA margin, and said Q1 FY27 would be sequentially stronger than Q4.

segments.name: CMT (Communications, Media & Technology)
segments.commentary: Sequential growth exceeded 7% in Q4; client expansions exploring Manila, Cairo and Fayetteville. Management is monitoring the proposed NPRM on offshore contact-centre restrictions.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Softer quarter with a couple of consulting engagements down; a European bank signed for client lifecycle work and is ramping up. FCC (financial crime and compliance) named as a pole-position area.

segments.name: High-Tech
segments.commentary: Budgets focused on transformation and automation; first Agentic AI deployments in Q4 were won here. Management is optimistic and expects higher growth in FY27.

segments.name: M&D and Retail
segments.commentary: Softer Q4 with a strong pipeline across new and existing accounts. Management is cautious on high-end fashion and retail.

segments.name: Emerging business (F&A, Personiv brand)
segments.commentary: Strong growth for three consecutive quarters, focused on SMB finance and accounting automation.

segments.name: Fashion & Luxury (CLX)
segments.commentary: Sluggish year; expected to return to growth in H1 FY27 on new GenAI wins at a key client and early green shoots, mostly from existing clients.

segments.name: Analytics & automation
segments.commentary: Order book of USD 90 million; management expects it to grow faster than company growth. Market360 named a Gartner representative vendor for Digital Shelf Analytics.

guidance_outlook: FY27: top-quartile operating revenue growth versus peers, reiterated; management declined to say whether FY27 growth will be lower or higher than FY26.
FY27 operating EBITDA margin guidance kept at 24% to 28%, same band as FY26; management declined to narrow it, though analysts had asked.
Q1 FY27 expected to be sequentially stronger than Q4 FY26; management did not say which half (H1 or H2) will be stronger.
FY26 EBITDA margin guidance was 24-28%, with a sequential EBITDA growth expectation.
Wage increments effective April 1; Q1 wage hike impact of about 300-350 bps, similar to FY26.
CLX expected to return to growth in H1 FY27.
Roll-offs expected to remain at 15-20% of revenue annually; management does not expect AI to change this much.
Subcontracting expected to grow in line with revenue, not faster.
Hedging: about 80% of USD receivables hedged, with the FY27 hedge book at about INR 89/USD, so FX upside is limited.
Dividend of INR 1 per share proposed; management said buybacks remain the preferred capital allocation option.
capex_capacity: Q4 capex increased, mainly on computers and networking equipment.
Utilization was 74% in Q4 FY26, down from the 76.5% eight-quarter high in Q3.
Headcount was added in Q4 with higher travel costs; management said Q1 headcount reflects expected sequential growth.
ESOP Trust bought about INR 250 crores of shares from the market in FY26 under the FY22 scheme (in place since 2015 scheme).
demand_pricing: Deal wins of USD 46 million in Q4 FY26; the trailing 12-month ACV was about USD 170 million, up from about USD 130-140 million a year ago (management's figures).
Management aspires to show YoY growth in bookings in FY27 but did not commit, citing AI-led deflation and competition in BPO/KPO and productised services.
First large-scale Agentic AI win in Q4 (consumer/retail per analyst), deployments from Q1 FY27 and ramp expected from Q4 FY27; commercial structure similar to other contracts.
Client billing rates and headcount per project: no meaningful change seen in Q4 or prior quarters, per management.
AI start-ups entering the market have not yet shown up meaningfully in client conversations or conversions.
Top 10 client concentration fell to 59% from 63-64%.

qa_highlights.question: Given the softer Q4 exit and strong FY26 order book, will FY27 growth momentum be lower than FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to say whether FY27 would be lower or higher, but reaffirmed top-quartile growth for the full year and said Q1 should be better sequentially than Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin guidance for FY27 the same as FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the 24-28% EBITDA band is retained; Q4 was in line with internal expectations and flagged at Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What was the FY26 margin walk?
qa_highlights.answer: Delivery and support employee cost broadly flat; G&A about 80 bps lower (facilities about 40 bps, other about 20 bps, tech about 10 bps); S&D about 20 bps lower. Total operating EBITDA expansion about 120 bps. FX impact was not answered and will be followed up.

qa_highlights.question: Why did subcontracting cost rise sharply as a percentage of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: A reclassification of some expenses from business promotion to subcontracting in the quarter, covering the full year; excluding this, the BAU ratio is in line with revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 hedge book a limit on FX upside?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; most of the hedge book is at about INR 89/USD for FY27, and about 80% of USD receivables are hedged, so upside is limited.

qa_highlights.question: Will bookings grow in FY27 and is USD 40-50M a quarter the new run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to YoY bookings growth but did not give a quarterly run rate; it cited deflation and competition as reasons for caution.

risks_watch: US NPRM on offshore contact-centre work could affect CMT clients; management is in contingency planning and says it is at an initial stage.
AI-led deflation in contract values, and whether bookings can grow YoY in FY27 as management aspires.
Quarterly volatility from deal timing; Q1 FY27 must be sequentially stronger than Q4 FY26.
Softer M&D, retail and high-end fashion; BFSI consulting engagements down.
Wage increments from April 1 (300-350 bps impact in Q1) against a 24-28% margin band.
Attrition at 21% and rising headcount with utilization down from 76.5% to 74%.
Regulatory changes in financial services affecting FCC demand.
Management did not specify which half will be stronger in FY27 and did not narrow guidance bands; analyst asked for broader band guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full year and the top-quartile growth target, but cautious on quarterly momentum and on AI-led deflation. Management avoided quantifying Agentic AI revenue and declined to narrow guidance or compare FY27 with FY26 growth.
key_quotes: So, on margin, yes, we would like to retain the same guidance between 24% to 28%.
AI is another productivity tool, and it takes time to implement.
We expect that it should definitely be better than what we did in Q4, if you look at the sequential growth.
Buybacks will continue to remain the preferred option.

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 top-quartile peer revenue growth and a 24-28% EBITDA margin, with Q1 FY27 guided sequentially stronger than Q4 (Q4 revenue only +0.6% QoQ), but no capacity additions were specified and utilisation fell to 74% from 76.5%, so backing is partial (deal wins of USD 46M, USD 90M analytics order book, CLX recovery in H1 FY27).
